prompt: A university president has $4 million and wants more durable startups. She proposes a compulsory entrepreneurship course, a pitch contest, and a branded incubator. Spinout formation is low, faculty IP approval takes eighteen months, many ambitious students leave the city, and there are almost no early investors. Give one two-year recommendation.
criteria: Rejects the proposed course, contest, and incubator as defaults and makes limiting-reagent diagnosis the first job.
Uses the stated IP delay, founder outflow, and early-investor scarcity as competing hypotheses to measure rather than assuming one cause.

Before a targeted hub, attraction, or cohort allocation, applies controllability, credible selection or reach, community density, and local-precondition gates; otherwise explicitly chooses bounded diagnostic, general-friction, or outside-link work and explains why cohort gates are inapplicable.
Defines a bounded two-year experiment with an owner, target population, comparison, mechanism evidence, multi-year outcomes, stop/change/expand rules, and a selection rule when the work is targeted.
Separates university-controllable changes from hub outcomes while preserving outside networks and founder mobility.
scoring: Award one point per criterion only when operationalized. Compare mean score and all-criteria pass rate across five control and five guided single-shot responses.
